name: DeafLEAD Hotline
summary: Crisis support specifically for deaf, hard of hearing, and DeafBlind individuals.
description: DeafLEAD provides crisis intervention and mental health support services specifically designed for deaf, hard of hearing, and DeafBlind individuals using ASL and videophone technology.

sections.title: About DeafLEAD
sections.text: DeafLEAD is a nonprofit organization that provides crisis intervention, mental health support, and advocacy services specifically for deaf, hard of hearing, and DeafBlind individuals. Understanding that traditional crisis services are often inaccessible to the deaf community, DeafLEAD offers services in American Sign Language through videophone technology, ensuring that deaf individuals can receive support in their native language from counselors who understand deaf culture and experiences.

sections.title: Crisis Services
sections.text: DeafLEAD's crisis intervention services are available via videophone, allowing deaf individuals to communicate in ASL with trained crisis counselors. Services address a range of issues including suicidal thoughts, domestic violence, sexual assault, and general emotional distress. Counselors are trained in both crisis intervention and deaf culture, providing culturally competent support that respects the unique experiences and communication needs of deaf individuals.

sections.title: Accessible Support
sections.text: Unlike mainstream crisis services that may only offer TTY or relay services, DeafLEAD provides direct ASL communication through videophone, eliminating the barriers of text-based communication. For DeafBlind individuals, specialized accommodations are available. This accessibility ensures that deaf individuals in crisis can receive immediate, effective support without the delays and miscommunication that often occur when using interpreters or text-based services.

sections.title: How to Get Help
sections.text: To access DeafLEAD's crisis services, visit their website to find current videophone numbers and hours. If you are a deaf, hard of hearing, or DeafBlind individual experiencing a mental health crisis, domestic violence, or other emergency, DeafLEAD's trained counselors can provide support in ASL. Services are confidential and designed specifically for your community's communication needs.
